Eric Barlow

Republican candidate for Governor, Wyoming · Open seat

Large-animal veterinarian, rancher, small business owner, and Wyoming state senator

Eric Barlow is a Republican state senator from Campbell County and a former Speaker of the Wyoming House. He announced his run for governor in August 2025, and he is the Republican nominee for the open seat. Gov. Mark Gordon, who cannot run again because of term limits, is leaving office.

Where Barlow stands

State budget
Supports cash-based budgeting and "right-sized government." Says programs that duplicate others, are outdated, or are not producing results should be scaled back, while core functions should keep the funding they need.
Public lands
Opposes the wholesale sale or broad transfer of Wyoming's public lands. He introduced SJ0009, a resolution reaffirming multiple use, public access, and locally driven land stewardship.
Data centers
Says local communities should decide on data center proposals. Says the state's role is to protect water resources, prevent higher electricity rates, and help communities get accurate information.
Healthcare
Proposes a healthcare strike team. His goals include more providers, stronger rural hospitals and clinics, support for EMS, more behavioral health capacity, better telehealth, price transparency, and training pathways for health workers.
Economic development and workforce
Says the state should not pick winners and losers. Supports workforce development through career and technical education, apprenticeships, and closer coordination among employers, schools, community colleges, and the University of Wyoming.
Government accessibility
Proposes regional governor's offices around the state, saying the best solutions come from the people closest to the issue.
Top priorities
Named education, healthcare, and water rights as top issues facing Wyoming, citing the Colorado River situation.

Background

  • Wyoming State Senate (current member)
  • Wyoming House of Representatives, five terms; served as Majority Leader and as Speaker
  • Large-animal veterinarian, rancher, and small business owner
  • Veterinary degree
  • U.S. Marine Corps veteran
  • Graduate of Campbell County High School; born in Gillette
